Abridged UMR 0.9 guidelines for Chinese and English at Stage 1 (numbered PropBank roles), with the names of the
UMR release data (`author`, `document-creation-time`, `full-affirmative`, `:modal-strength`, `:refer-person`).

A UMR has two levels.

- **Sentence level**: one rooted, directed graph per sentence in PENMAN notation, adapted from AMR:
  concepts (events, entities, abstract concepts), the relations between them (participant roles and
  non-participant roles) and attributes (aspect, polarity, mode, quantity, pe...
edit.new: A UMR has one graph per sentence (PENMAN, adapted from AMR) and document-level temporal, modal and coreference relations.

edit.old: - Precision counts as much as recall: when a link is not clear, leave it out.

- Before the next sentence, check the graph: every meaningful word has its concept, every event its aspect, every
  role the right direction; at the end check the document-level relations cover every event and entity.
- Within one sentence, coreference is a re-entrancy in the graph (one variable), not a `:coref` triple.
edit.new: - Within one sentence, a pronoun (also 他们/*they* for an organisation or publication) or a dropped argument re-uses its antecedent's variable, no own node; a possessive pronoun on an event nominal is omitted. An overt repeated name or noun (short name, bare head noun) gets its own node plus a `:same-...

edit.text: With 但是/不过/却 later in the same sentence, 虽然/尽管 gives `but-91 :ARG1 <concessive clause(s)> :ARG2 <main clause>` instead.

UMR release data also marks it with `:quote <reporting event>` when the content is a quotation.
edit.new: The reported content's top event, and each of its conjuncts, always gets `:quote <reporting event>` (also passive 被指/被称); a quoted slogan's content gets `:quote` on its framing node.

edit.text: nor for 还/也 right after it; a dropped subject of the later clause re-enters the first clause's subject.

edit.old: - Coreference across sentences is in `:coref`; within a sentence it is a re-entrancy.
edit.new: - Same-sentence pronouns are re-entrancies, repeated nouns own nodes + `:coref`; control subjects re-enter nominal complements; a time over both halves of but-91 attaches to both.

edit.text: Frequency adverbs (经常, 常常, 往往, 重复; *often, repeatedly*) are `:frequency`.

edit.anchor: The place rule holds for abstract nouns too.
edit.text: Every location postposition likewise: 在 N 中/上/里 → `(z / 中 :op1 N)`. Check the roleset for a location argument (出现-type) before using `:place`.

edit.new: A named human or character, fictional too, is `individual-person`. A bare category noun right before a name (no 的, no title) is the type concept, not an apposition.

edit.new: Pick one anchor event (the main eventive predicate; in a coordination, the first conjunct's)
